message.content: {"caption":"A curriculum agent’s three sample questions are shown beside an agent’s worked solution and Python check for an alternating-sum problem.","description":"The figure is a two-column infographic with rounded text panels. On the left, under “Generated Questions from Curriculum Agent,” three blue panels are arranged vertically and labeled Iter 1, Iter 2, and Iter 3. Small cartoon agent/robot avatars sit beside the iteration labels. Iter 1 asks: Given triangle ABC with ∠A = 90°, points D and E on sides AB and AC respectively, and AD + EC = BC and AD · EC = BD · AE, find ∠B. Iter 2 asks: A rectangle R has side lengths 10 and 5. A point P inside it has distances x, y, 10 − x, and 5 − y from its four sides, where x and y are positive real numbers; find the maximum possible value of x² + y². Iter 3 describes a city with distinct integer neighborhood addresses from 1 to N. A parade route must visit all neighborhoods, and consecutive addresses on the route must not share any digit. For example, after starting at address 15, the next stop cannot have either 1 or 5 in its address. It asks for the maximum N and requests a three-digit answer. The panels contain text only; there are no arrows or connecting lines between them.\n\nOn the right, an orange-outlined panel headed “Test Question (MATH)” asks to compute 1 − 2 + 3 − 4 + 5 − … + 99 − 100. Below, a larger green-outlined panel headed “Model Output by Agent0,” with a small agent avatar, explains that the terms alternate in sign and groups them as (1 − 2) + (3 − 4) + (5 − 6) + … + (99 − 100). It says each pair (2k − 1) − 2k equals −1, that 100 terms make 50 pairs, and therefore the sum is 50 × (−1) = −50. A gray code area shows Python code that sums i when i is odd and −i when it is even for i from 1 through 100, then prints the result. Its output is −50, and the concluding sentence gives the sum as boxed −50. A small tool/agent illustration appears by the code heading. The panels are adjacent but have no arrows or other explicit connections.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
